subject: RBAC shadow membership — discrepancy in SCIM sync (SOC 2 evidence)
messages:
From: Julie Hart <julie.hart@healthsync.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected admin assignments after SCIM sync

Hi Marissa —

Our SOC 2 auditor (BrightAudit) flagged a sample of accounts that appear to have been granted admin-level roles following the nightly SCIM sync on 2025-06-20. We picked three accounts that should have been provisioned with 'user' only, but show 'org_admin' in the RBAC snapshot.

Quick details:
- Sample accounts: julie.hart, c.mendes, onboarding-test-17
- SCIM delta id: 2025-06-20T14:22Z (we were given this by BrightAudit)
- Auditor notes: "27 of 500 sampled memberships show higher-than-expected privileges; cause unknown"

Can you provide the SCIM delta export (for that token) and the RBAC snapshot for 06/20–06/28? Auditor needs evidence that role assignments are consistent with SCIM attributes and that no elevation occurred from SAML assertions.

We also need a short narrative we can include in the SOC 2 pack explaining remediation steps if an anomaly is confirmed.

Thanks — Julie
Julie Hart
Security & Compliance, HealthSync
julie.hart@healthsync.com

[Attachment: sample_audit_extract.csv (CSV, 12KB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Julie Hart <julie.hart@healthsync.com>
Cc: sean.gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 29 Jun 2025 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected admin assignments after SCIM sync

Hi Julie — thanks for the heads-up.

I'm looping in Sean (infra/authorization) to pull the SCIM delta and RBAC snapshot you requested. A couple clarifying questions to make sure we hand over the right artifacts:

1) Is BrightAudit asking for the raw SCIM patch file for the delta id you provided (2025-06-20T14:22Z) or a processed CSV that maps SCIM attribute -> role changes?
2) Do you want SAML assertion samples for the three accounts listed (in case the role came from IdP claims)?

Plan: Sean will pull the RBAC snapshot (service-account and human accounts), and a SCIM/CMD audit bundle. We will redact any personally identifiable telemetry that isn't relevant to the SOC 2 sample. Expect an initial bundle by EOD tomorrow (Mon 06/30).

If you need faster turnaround we can prioritize the three sample accounts and hand those over today.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Security Liaison, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, irene.choi@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 29 Jun 2025 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected admin assignments after SCIM sync

Marissa / Irene —

I pulled an initial set of artifacts and staged them in S3 (read-only link below). Attachments below are a small curated set we can share with the auditor:

- rbac_snapshot_20250628.json (full snapshot, 1.2MB, service accounts + human users)
- scim_delta_20250620.csv (flattened CSV: uid, op, attrs_changed, old_roles, new_roles)
- saml_assertion_samples.txt (three assertions for the sample accounts, with timestamps)

S3 path (internal): s3://redwood-prod-logs/scim/deltas/2025/06/20/ (we staged the CSV there)
Drive share (external-ready, redacted): https://drive.redwood.com/notes/SCIM-investigation-57821
HubSpot ticket: HUBSPOT-57821

Observations from a quick scan:
- The SCIM patch for 2025-06-20 contains a batch with a mix of 'replace' and 'add' ops where the incoming attribute 'role' was set to 'admin' for a small subset. The source for those patches is our SCIM sync connector from HealthSync (look for connector_id: hs-connector-17).
- There is one service account (svc-deploy-bot) that had an escalation path to a role mapping template; that template was recently edited (2025-06-19) with a looser mapping for name patterns.
- I have not yet found SAML assertions that independently conferred admin privileges — the three sample assertions show typical group claims, not direct role grant claims.

Command I ran to extract members with source=scim and admin role:
SELECT uid, role, source, last_modified FROM rbac_members WHERE source = 'scim' AND role IN ('org_admin','admin');

Next steps I propose:
1) Produce the redacted SCIM CSV and RBAC snapshot for external delivery (I put the files in Drive and staged S3).
2) Irene — can you pull the SAML assertion logs for the three accounts (timestamps included in the CSV) and drop to the shared Drive? We should include a short note saying whether assertions contained role claims.
3) Marissa — I can prepare a short remediation narrative around the template change + mitigation steps (revert template, add pattern guardrails, add a locked mapping for svc accounts).

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com

[Attachment: rbac_snapshot_20250628.json (JSON, 1.2MB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Julie Hart <julie.hart@healthsync.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected admin assignments after SCIM sync

Hi Julie — following up with the artifacts and a short narrative for your SOC 2 package.

What we delivered:
- scim_delta_20250620.csv (flattened, showing the batch where role attribute was set to 'admin' for ~27 accounts). Attached and posted to Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/notes/SCIM-investigation-57821
- rbac_snapshot_20250628.json (snapshot of our RBAC table as of 2025-06-28). Attached.
- saml_assertion_samples.txt (three SAML assertions for the sample accounts; Irene confirmed no assertion included a direct role claim). Attached.

Root cause (summary):
- A change to an internal role-mapping template (applied 2025-06-19) expanded a pattern that matched some HealthSync usernames and introduced an unintended mapping to admin-type roles during the SCIM processing batch on 2025-06-20.

Remediation steps taken:
1) Rolled back the role-mapping template to the prior safe version (complete)
2) Removed the inadvertent admin role from the affected accounts (manual rollback + automated revert for matching pattern)
3) Added a pre-flight validation to the SCIM processing pipeline that rejects tokenized template changes which would map external identities to admin roles without an explicit allowlist
4) Added a short guardrail in the console and an alert to infra-runbook so changes to role templates trigger a peer-review and a dry-run in staging.

Attached files should satisfy the auditor's request; BrightAudit requested the CSV and snapshot plus a narrative which we've included above. If BrightAudit wants the raw SCIM patch batch (not the flattened CSV), we can provide the raw file from S3 under the same Drive share (HUBSPOT-57821).

Let me know if you need the raw SCIM patch or additional logs for more accounts — we can expand the sample set.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Customer Security Liaison, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

[Attachments: scim_delta_20250620.csv, rbac_snapshot_20250628.json, saml_assertion_samples.txt]
